messages:
priya: Heads-up — incoming billing escalation for a private/VPC deployment. Customer reports invoice shows ~120k tokens higher than their audit logs for 2026-03-10 14:00-14:10 UTC. They run meter-agent v1.8.2 on k8s with a 5s shutdown grace period.

priya: I pulled our aggregator ingress and the agent relay logs. I see repeated POSTs that responded 502 followed by a few `failed to inflate` errors. Suspect truncated gzipped batches on pod termination.

infra-bot: [alert] 2026-03-10T14:05:12Z aggregator: POST /private/meter 502 (payload_len=1024, recv_len=512)

leo: Can you paste the agent log around that time? need the exact error lines and header details (content-encoding, content-length).

priya: Pasted snippet from /var/log/meter-agent/relay.log: 
```
2026-03-10T14:05:11Z INFO batching: flushing 48 events (uncompressed=45KB, compressed=1.0KB)
2026-03-10T14:05:11Z INFO http: POST https://aggregator.private.internal/v1/meter (gzip=true, content-length=1024)
2026-03-10T14:05:12Z ERROR http: unexpected EOF while inflating response: unexpected EOF
2026-03-10T14:05:12Z ERROR relay: upload incomplete, bytes_sent=512, expected=1024
2026-03-10T14:05:12Z WARN lifecycle: received SIGTERM, graceful shutdown remaining=0s
```

priya: Note the pod got SIGTERM and remaining grace window was 0s (k8s evicted). Looks like the agent started the HTTP upload but was terminated mid-stream; aggregator recorded a partial payload and ingested what it could, leading to an inconsistent ledger vs audit log.

billing-bot: Invoices: customer_ACME (acct-1045) invoice 2026-03 shows +118,934 extra tokens in window 14:04-14:06 UTC. Our ingestion timestamp matches the partial batches in aggregator.

sam: That matches a class of issues we've not seen in v1.8.x: batcher compresses payload then streams it; if the process exits before flush finishes the HTTP body can be truncated but server may have already parsed/accepted a portion. We should check preStop hook + reduce batch window or ensure flush on SIGTERM blocks until upload finished.

leo: Repro plan: run a local agent with small batched window (50 events), start an HTTP sink that accepts gzip but intentionally closes connection after 512 bytes. Kill the agent with kill -TERM while upload in-flight. See if aggregator creates partial records. Jordan, can you run on the repro cluster?

jordan: Running now. Quick command I'm using: 
```bash
# run fake aggregator that truncates mid-body
python3 -m http.server --bind 0.0.0.0 8080 --cgi &
# simple truncation handler in python to accept connection and then close after n bytes (iterating)
```

jordan: Repro confirmed: when agent is SIGTERM'd during upload we see a broken gzip stream, agent logs show "upload incomplete" and aggregator created a partial batch entry (seq range 23920-23967) where later events lost token counts.

priya: Customer-facing impact: their internal audit (event-level ledger) shows fewer tokens than our invoice because the partial ingestion path counted tokens differently (server-side heuristics filled in missing fields). They flagged it as overbilling.

leo: Short-term mitigation: 1) immediate reconciliation: subtract tokens for affected batch window from next invoice (manual credit) 2) patch agent to block in preStop: wait up to X seconds for inflight uploads to finish and retry on transient errors 3) add server-side validation to reject truncated gzip payloads (return 400) instead of accepting partial.

sam: Also add a k8s PodDisruptionBudget note in docs: dont use 0s terminationGracePeriod for onprem setups running agent. Recommend >=30s.

jordan: I exported affected seq ranges and token totals. Attaching quick summary (from our audit): 
```
affected_window: 2026-03-10T14:04:50Z - 2026-03-10T14:05:30Z
aggregator_count: 1,217,984 tokens
customer_audit_count: 1,099,050 tokens
delta: +118,934 tokens
batches_involved: 3 (seq: 23905-23972)
```

priya: Action owners: leo -> prepare hotfix that ensures upload fully completes on SIGTERM + retries; sam -> doc update about terminationGracePeriod recommendation; jordan -> coordinate credit with billing and customer success; I'll draft the support reply and the internal RCA.

leo: Hotfix notes: change shutdown path to flush synchronously and set http client with chunked upload + confirm server returns 200 only after full body validated. Also add a metric `agent.upload.truncated` to catch future occurrences.

billing-bot: Marking invoice for acct-1045 as disputed and creating a credit memo draft for -118,934 tokens pending engineering confirmation.

priya: Draft reply to customer: "we found an edge case where compressed meter payloads could be truncated during pod termination, causing an overcount on our side. We're issuing a credit for the difference while we deploy a fix and will follow up with a postmortem." Will share draft in #support-summaries.

sam: Will also open a follow-up change in the private deployment helm chart to set terminationGracePeriodSeconds=30 by default (opt-out).

leo: I'll backport fix to v1.8.x and include a small test that simulates truncated gzips in CI.

priya: Thanks all — I'll update thread when credit is issued and when the hotfix is deployed to affected customer's cluster. :white_check_mark:
